page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge belongs to the general-purpose compute family, leveraging the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading, reaching maximum clock speeds of 3.9 GHz. It features a substantial cache hierarchy encompassing 480 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is 256 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, establishing a standard 4 GB per vCPU ratio. No discrete GPU hardware is included.

This instance includes no local storage, directing all file and operational systems to utilize remote network volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 15 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default. The absence of local solid-state drives positions this instance primarily for networked compute and storage topologies rather than IOPS-heavy local disk operations.

Benchmark metrics indicate strong multi-threaded compute capability, achieving a multi-core stress-ng rating of 69,359.48 and a PassMark CPU score of 83,187.08. Geekbench evaluations reveal top-tier execution in Clang code compilation and image processing, supported by static web serving throughput exceeding 105 GB/s and strong Redis operations exceeding 114 million operations per second. Because the flex designation utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model, workloads demanding sustained maximum core utilization may experience performance variability compared to non-flex dedicated tiers.

By offering a burstable processing profile, the m8i-flex.16xlarge delivers qualitative cost efficiency over fully provisioned general-purpose instances when resource demands fluctuate. The balance of 256 GB RAM, matrix computation instructions, and 64 vCPUs makes it suitable for large-scale web serving, CI/CD compilation clusters, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks that operate on variable utilization cycles.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor reaching clock speeds of 3.9 GHz. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor with burstable CPU allocation, the system provides 256 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512 and AMX matrix accelerators. Bundled local storage is absent, requiring external volume attachments for persistent disks, while network interfaces deliver a 15 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark testing reflects top-tier capabilities in Clang software compilation, image processing, and static web serving, alongside strong multi-core computation and Redis throughput. The flex tier provides a cost-effective alternative to fixed-performance general-purpose instances for non-sustained or elastic processing. This server is suitable for enterprise web serving, software build pipelines, memory-resident key-value caching, and moderate machine learning inference workloads.
